questions.q: How did Leonardo change the standing of artists, according to the summary?
a: His fame and royal commissions made painters respected as thinkers
He made artwork cheap enough for ordinary people to buy
He ended the system of commissioned portraits and statues
He separated painting from science for the first time
questions.why: The first lesson says that only when Leonardo became famous and was hired by kings were artists respected for their creativity.

questions.q: What did Leonardo begin at age fourteen?
a: An apprenticeship with an artist and engineer
A university course in anatomy and medicine
A monastery school devoted to religious painting
A workshop run by a wealthy merchant family
questions.why: At fourteen he started an apprenticeship under Andrea del Verrocchio, who worked as both an artist and an engineer.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by calling Leonardo an expert generalist?
a: He linked many fields, using art to study anatomy and engineering
He mastered one subject before briefly trying another
He avoided finishing projects so he could keep exploring
He relied on assistants to handle the technical work
questions.why: The second lesson describes how he changed thinking across painting, anatomy, medicine and engineering, and infused random interests into his work.

questions.q: What happened to Leonardo's notebooks after his death?
a: They sat unread for centuries and slowed medical progress
They were printed at once and inspired working surgeons
They were destroyed by the patrons who commissioned him
They were translated and taught in universities across Europe
questions.why: The summary says the notes gathered dust for hundreds of years, and the mechanics of fluids in the heart were understood only 450 years later.

questions.q: What does the author suggest you do with your biggest ideas?
a: Write them down for posterity and leave a way to find them
Keep them private until every detail is fully worked out
Publish them early so rivals cannot claim them first
Share them only with a small circle of trusted peers
questions.why: The third lesson suggests writing your most important ideas down for future readers, so they can outlive you.
